teaser.text: AstraZeneca is a pharmaceutical company: it turns scientific discoveries into prescription medicines and sells them through a healthcare system that sits between the company and the patient. To understand its business, follow a medicine from diagnosis to factory to payer, then follow the dollar back through research, manufacturing and partners.

blocks.heading: Where could AstraZeneca's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted forecast points to moderate shareholder returns, with substantial execution risk. It reaches 12,571.74 GBp in October 2027, an 8% return including dividends, from today’s 11,892.00 GBp. It reaches 13,131.37 GBp in October 2028, a 15% return, and 13,714.80 GBp in October 2029, a 22% return.

The October 2029 range is wide: 6,541.08 GBp in the bear case to 22,391.36 GBp in the bull case. That spread reflects uncertainty over mature-product erosion, pipeline adoption, margins and the valuation multiple.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for AstraZeneca?

paragraphs.text: The October 2029 range runs from 6,541.08 GBp in the bear case to 22,391.36 GBp in the bull case. The base case is 13,820.47 GBp. Farxiga erosion and China price cuts must be offset by newer medicines during 2027–2029. Launch adoption, testing, reimbursement and sustained net revenue will decide whether the 2030 goals hold. Debt maturities in Q1 and Q2 2027 will compete with research, construction and launches for cash or refinancing capacity.

paragraphs.text: The dividend begins at $3.30 in FY2026, which management intends to declare under its progressive policy. The base case reaches $3.60 by FY2029, bear reaches $3.39, and bull reaches $3.95. The declared interim dividend of $1.06 supports continuation, but investment and deal payments keep base growth below earnings growth.

The forecast moves toward the bear case if Farxiga generic competition and China price cuts slow revenue during 2027–2029. Weak trial results, restrictive coverage or poor testing and prescribing would reduce launch revenue and the P/E; technical approval alone may not create broad patient use. Investment running ahead of cash generation would add debt while buybacks remain absent.

earnings.title: AstraZeneca earnings: guidance and what to watch
earnings.meta_description: AstraZeneca's next results are expected on October 30, 2026; see guidance, recent results and the pipeline events that matter.
earnings.opening: AstraZeneca's next results are expected on October 30, 2026. Watch whether newer medicines replace revenue lost when older products lose exclusivity.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how AstraZeneca's business works, who its rivals are, how management is paid and what risks it faces.

paragraphs.text: Its 2026 outlook says earnings per share should grow faster than revenue. “Core” earnings are management’s adjusted view of ordinary performance; reported earnings include costs such as acquired-asset write-downs and certain legal charges. Constant-currency growth holds exchange rates steady, so currency movements do not disguise changes in demand.

The longer promise is at least 20 new medicines and $80 billion in annual revenue by 2030. Starting from 2025 revenue of $58.739 billion, that requires about 6.4% yearly growth. Etcamah was the eleventh medicine counted toward the launch ambition, but an approval is only permission to sell. Patients must be identified, treated and reimbursed before a launch becomes substantial revenue.

blocks.heading: Has AstraZeneca kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: AstraZeneca promised annual revenue above $45 billion by 2023 while defending its independence during Pfizer’s takeover approach. It delivered $45.811 billion in 2023, although the result included Alexion. The newer ambition is $80 billion of revenue by 2030, adjusted for development risk and not dependent on future acquisitions. That makes the next test more revealing.

blocks.heading: How have AstraZeneca's revenue and profit changed?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose **6.4%** to **$15,384 million**. Gross margin improved from **82.9%** to **83.6%**, so the pressure appeared below gross profit. Operating income fell from **$3,508 million** to **$3,164 million**, as higher research and administrative spending and **$345 million** of development-asset impairments weighed on the quarter.

Net income still rose to **$2,507 million**, while diluted EPS reached **$1.61**. The reported tax rate fell to about **10%** from about **22%**, which helped offset the weaker operating result. Core operating income improved, so the quarter contains both commercial progress and weaker reported expense performance.
